children: Memory-chip maker Micron Technology Inc. (MU, Financials) is heading toward results with a lot greater challenge than whether it can surpass Wall Street projections.

Has the business really been altered by AI? That question is hard to overlook with Micron's third-quarter figures. Revenue increased to $41.46 billion from $9.30 billion a year earlier while gross margin increased to 84.9% from 39%.
Adjusted earnings came to $25.11 per share.

Management is guiding for fourth-quarter revenue of approximately $50 billion and gross margin of 86%. Wall Street is already in agreement, with consensus projections at about $50.4 billion in revenue and $30.89 in adjusted earnings per share.
That implies surpassing expectations may not be enough by itself. The larger clue may be Micron's guidance for high-bandwidth memory, pricing and fiscal 2027.

This time, says investor Sharon McArd, AI has made memory a more strategic aspect of the data-center infrastructure. Micron has also signed about $22 billion in client agreements, including take-or-pay contracts that give more visibility into demand.
Expectations are already high, and Sept. 30 will put Micron's outsized stats to the test: are they just another memory bubble, or something more permanent?

title: Micron's AI boom faces a much tougher earnings test
